chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, who said: Sa'd ibn 'Amr al-Zuhri narrated to us, who said: Bakr ibn Salim narrated to us from his father, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).

Regarding His saying, 'And she carried Him and withdrew with Him to a remote place,' he said: 'She went out from Damascus until she reached Karbala, and placed Him in the location of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), then she returned on the same night.'

And from him, from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Sa'id, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Basri, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: 'In the clay/mud of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is the cure from every disease, and it is the greatest medicine.'

key_terms.طِينِ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The clay or mud from the grave of Imam al-Husayn.
key_terms.كَرْبَلَاءَ: Karbala, a city in Iraq, site of the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn.
key_terms.مَكَاناً قَصِيًّا: A remote place, referring to the Quranic description of Maryam's withdrawal.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of the clay from the grave of Imam al-Husayn in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* presents a unique Shia exegetical view where Maryam’s 'remote place' (Qaswa) is identified as Karbala, linking the purity of the Prophetess to the sanctity of Imam al-Husayn’s burial site. The second part establishes the clay of his grave as *al-dawa al-akbar* (the greatest medicine), a concept that underpins the Shia practice of *Turbat al-Husayn* for healing and prayer, reflecting the belief in the spiritual efficacy of the Ahl al-Bayt's physical remains.
